key_insight: Four vision backbones reached similar brain tumour segmentation performance through different internal changes, showing that comparable task scores can mask differences in cross-task transfer.
clinical_relevance: For medical imaging research, backbone and adaptation-layer selection may help preserve performance across tasks rather than optimise segmentation alone.
method: LoRA-adapted DINOv3, SigLIP2, MerMED-FM and BiomedCLIP for brain tumour segmentation.
Probed internal changes using attention divergence, weight-change analysis and activation patching.
Restricted LoRA to causally relevant early-to-mid layers and compared with full-layer adaptation.
evidence_signal: Across six datasets covering segmentation and Alzheimer's disease classification, mean segmentation Dice was 78–81%; adaptation improved classification for DINOv3 but degraded it for the other three backbones.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish prospective clinical performance or whether the layer-selection strategy generalises beyond the studied backbones and tasks.
paper_title: Convergent Performance, Divergent Mechanisms in LoRA-Adapted Vision Foundation Models for Brain MRI
